subject: Marketplace vs Direct: procurement path, billing & compliance questions
messages:

Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace vs Direct — procurement questions for Redwood

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Procurement here at FinSecure is trying to decide whether we should purchase Redwood via the AWS Marketplace (Private Offer) or pursue a direct contract / invoice route with your sales team. Our main concerns are:

- Invoicing cadence and PO process (we prefer monthly vs prepaid annual licenses)
- Data residency and SOC 2 artifacts for auditors
- Whether AWS Marketplace will affect co-sell discounts/partner incentives for our account

Can you outline the practical differences we should expect from an operational standpoint? Also, any timelines or docs we can provide to our internal legal/procurement would be helpful.

Appreciate a short summary we can share with our procurement lead.

Best,
Alex
Alex Doe
Sr. Procurement Manager
FinSecure

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.example.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace vs Direct — procurement questions for Redwood

Alex —

Great questions, thank you. High level summary first, then practical notes for procurement/legal. I attached a short price/comparison spreadsheet (redwood_price_compare_aws_vs_direct_20270628.xlsx) that shows differences for this deal profile.

Quick summary:
- AWS Marketplace (Private Offer): fastest procurement path if you want Marketplace billing (invoice via AWS). Supports private offers so you get negotiated pricing and AWS handles invoicing. Good if you want to keep vendor management through AWS and need faster procurement approval.
- Direct contract (Redwood invoice): Redwood issues invoices directly, supports monthly billing, and allows custom billing terms (net30/net45) and PO flow. Slightly longer setup for legal/msa signatures if you require our commercial MSA.

Operational considerations:
- Invoicing & PO: Marketplace invoices come from AWS; we can set the private offer to be annual prepay or subscription monthly depending on partner settings — for monthly chargebacks we'll usually set up a subscription-based private offer. Direct route lets us invoice monthly and attach your POs directly to our billing.
- Co-sell / incentives: If you want to keep AWS co-sell incentives, we can do a Marketplace private offer and still enable co-sell via the partner/ISV process. There are timing and revenue attribution nuances (we can share the partner opportunity ID). If you go direct and want AWS credit/co-sell, we can coordinate but it requires additional registration steps.
- Security & compliance: Both routes support our SOC 2 report and standard security artifacts. For Marketplace purchases, customers still accept our SOC 2 letter and we can provide evidence via a secured SharePoint or AWS Artifact link (per your preference).
- Contract redlines: Marketplace private offers reduce the amount of redline negotiation on payment terms; direct contracts allow more flexibility with SLAs and indemnity language but will extend legal review.

Recommended next steps for FinSecure procurement:
1) If speed to production and simpler procurement oversight is primary: choose AWS Marketplace Private Offer. We (Redwood) will create a private offer and share the DocuSign link and the private-offer ID to your AWS account.
2) If you require specific contractual language or monthly invoicing directly to a PO with custom billing terms: proceed with a direct Redwood MSA and monthly invoicing; expect 7–14 business days for legal + billing setup.

I attached the comparison sheet and a one page checklist you can drop into your RFP. Happy to jump on a 20-min call with procurement/legal to walk through.

Regards,

Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales (Marketplace & GTM)
Redwood Inference

3) For co-sell recognition: if we go Marketplace, will FinSecure still qualify for any discounts you might extend for co-sell referrals through AWS? We want to make sure our procurement choice doesn't unintentionally disqualify us from partner-driven incentives.

If it's easier, we can schedule a short call with your billing/legal folks.

Soojin / Lauren / Alex —

Confirmed — operational recommendation below.

Short answers:
- Monthly billing via AWS Marketplace Private Offer: YES. We can configure a monthly subscription private offer tied to the customer's AWS account so FinSecure will get monthly AWS invoices and be able to allocate spend monthly. Caveat: depending on the AWS marketplace configuration for the private offer, some billing reconciliation steps are routed through AWS and revenue attribution to Redwood happens on AWS's cadence.
- DPA & SOC 2 artifacts: YES. Purchasing via Marketplace does not prevent us from executing our DPA (we will provide a signed DPA separately). SOC 2 evidence can be shared through a secure link or via AWS Artifact if needed. For audits, we typically provide a named contact and a short evidence package (report, scope, controls list).
- Co-sell / discounts: We can preserve co-sell attribution with a Marketplace private offer but we must register the opportunity with the AWS Partner team prior to close (we'll provide the partner opportunity ID). If FinSecure needs a co-sell discount applied, we'll encode the negotiated price into the private offer. Note: some partner incentives are subject to AWS reporting windows; please allow 4–8 weeks for partner crediting to complete after the private offer is accepted.

Recommended route (balance of speed and contractual control):
1) Proceed with AWS Marketplace Private Offer configured as a monthly subscription — this satisfies FinSecure finance for monthly allocation and keeps procurement fast.
2) Redwood will: (a) create a private offer with the negotiated price, (b) share the DocuSign private-offer acceptance link, (c) execute the DPA outside of Marketplace and provide SOC2 evidence via secure share, and (d) register the opportunity with AWS partner team for co-sell attribution.

Next steps for FinSecure procurement:
- We (Redwood) will create the private offer and send a DocuSign link (target: within 48 hours).
- FinSecure signs the private offer in DocuSign and provides the AWS Account ID for offer targeting.
- We register the opportunity with AWS and confirm partner attribution.
